faq.q: What is the best free iOS app for planning a motorcycle trip?
faq.a: VisorUp is our pick for free trip planning on iPhone. You can build a custom route with road preferences, plan a multi-day tour with day breaks, see automatic fuel stops from 9,913 UK stations, work through an interactive packing checklist, add curated points of interest and export the whole thing as a GPX file. It is free and ad-free, so it covers the core planning job without pushing you to a subscription.

faq.q: How do I track and record my motorcycle rides on iPhone?
faq.a: VisorUp's Live Ride Mode tracks your ride stats as you go. For dedicated logging, Scenic is a well-liked iOS ride recorder that plots your route and lets you attach photos, and Relive creates a 3D flyover video from your GPS track that is great for sharing. Between them you can plan, navigate, record and relive an entire tour from your phone.

faq.q: What is a GPX file and why does it matter?
faq.a: A GPX file is a standard format for storing a route or track. Exporting your plan as GPX means you can share it with friends over WhatsApp, email or AirDrop, and load it into other apps or a dedicated GPS. VisorUp exports GPX from any route you build. Our guide on how to use GPX files explains the whole workflow.

faq.q: Which apps help me find biker-friendly places to stay?
faq.a: Booking.com has the widest selection of B&Bs, hotels and guesthouses with instant booking and reviews, and you can filter for parking. Pitchup is the go-to for UK campsites with availability and facilities. Whichever you use, message the property to confirm secure motorcycle parking, as listings do not always make this clear.

faq.q: Do I still need to plan fuel and stops if an app does routing?
faq.a: Yes. VisorUp plans fuel stops automatically, which is a huge help, but you should still sanity-check ranges and opening hours for genuinely remote areas such as the north-west Highlands, where a station may be closed on a Sunday. Treat the app's plan as a strong starting point and confirm the critical stops yourself before a long or remote day.

content:
Plan the Trip Before You Turn a Wheel

The best tours are made at the kitchen table, not the roadside. A little planning, the route, the fuel, the weather window, the stops and somewhere to sleep, is the difference between a relaxed adventure and a stressful scramble. Your iPhone makes that planning quick and visual, and most of the tools you need are free. This guide covers the best iOS apps for planning motorcycle trips and tracking your rides in the UK for 2026, and how to fit them together into a simple workflow.

Route and Trip Building: VisorUp

Start with VisorUp, which was built for exactly this. Its route builder uses drag-and-drop waypoints and a road-preference control, so you can shape a route around fast progress or the twistiest roads you can find. It plans automatic fuel stops from a database of 9,913 UK stations, lets you add any of 1,889 curated points of interest with one tap, and supports multi-day trip planning with sensible day breaks. There is a weather overlay for choosing your window, an interactive packing checklist so nothing gets forgotten, and GPX export so the finished plan can be shared with your group. It is free with no ads. For the full feature picture, see our roundup of the best iOS apps for motorcycle riding.

Detailed Route Planning: RideWithGPS

RideWithGPS is a powerful route planner with elevation profiles, which is genuinely useful when a route crosses mountain passes and you want to understand the gradients involved. It is popular across cycling and motorcycling, exports GPX cleanly, and its premium tier adds offline maps and turn-by-turn. Use it alongside VisorUp when you want to study a route in fine detail before committing.

Ride Recording: Scenic and Relive

Recording a ride is half the fun. Scenic is a motorcycle-specific iOS app that records your route, plots it on a map and builds shareable ride logs with photos attached, with a modest premium tier (around £10 a year). Relive takes your GPS track and turns it into a 3D flyover video, which is a brilliant way to share a tour on social media. VisorUp's Live Ride Mode also tracks your ride stats in real time, so you can keep recording lightweight and let the dedicated apps do the fancy output.

Accommodation: Booking.com and Pitchup

For beds, Booking.com has the largest selection of B&Bs, hotels and guesthouses with instant booking, reviews and parking filters. For canvas, Pitchup is the leading UK campsite finder with availability, facilities and prices. Park4Night, though aimed at campervans, is handy for finding overnight stopping places on the move. Whatever you book, message ahead to confirm secure motorcycle parking, which listings rarely state clearly. Our guides to camping versus hotels and biker-friendly campsites go deeper on choosing where to stay.

Weather and Timing

Timing a UK trip around the weather is a skill in itself. Use the Met Office app for accurate forecasts and warnings and Windy to watch systems move, then pick your day. VisorUp's weather overlay helps you sense-check conditions along the route rather than just at your destination, which matters when you are crossing high ground.

A Simple iOS Planning Workflow

  • Shape the route in VisorUp with your chosen road preference and day breaks.
  • Add stops from the curated points of interest, and let the app plan fuel.
  • Study the detail in RideWithGPS if the route crosses serious terrain.
  • Book beds with Booking.com or Pitchup, confirming parking directly.
  • Check the weather window with the Met Office and Windy.
  • Export GPX and share the plan with your group before you leave.
  • Record the ride with Scenic or Relive so you can relive it afterwards.

Do this once and it becomes second nature. The planning takes an evening, costs nothing, and turns a vague idea into a tour you will actually enjoy riding. When you are ready to load your plan onto the bike, our guide on how to use GPX files covers the final step.
